prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M; grid, port out of scope. Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment); Main Transformer; Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher if capability<target or changes; applies Dispatcher ceiling, Grid Constraint response). Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss; fire shutdown; keeps local protection if supervisory link lost), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Export Cable Monitor (alarms→Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start; Start Test Trace→Substation Operator); both never bypassed. Helideck. Modes: Degraded (records function, condition, time; safety over production/schedule; escalate beyond envelope), Substation Degraded (protection/aux/monitoring impairment), Grid Constraint, Weather Hold (Weather Service, Weather Analyst), Vessel Standby (marine reduced), Turbine Lockout (safety-critical fault until assessed/authorized; no remote restart in fire). Recovery: cause corrected/bounded, operator confirms stable, checks before automatic; Control Engineer coordinates before lifting restrictions, suspends unconfirmed remote commands. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard; status, restrictions→Duty Planner). Alarms: safety>protection>export. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; records→Shore Control Room; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway; preserves status); SCADA Engineer investigates indications. Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; holds last limit). Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale; separates safety-critical work). Operations Radio Console (CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft). Personnel Tracking Console. Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note→Duty Planner. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation; with Vessel Master confirms accountability. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction→Personnel Tracking Console. Recovery Basket Load Sheet→Rescue Coordinator. HSE Officer: evacuation advice; reviews workarounds. Field Supervisor: work status→Shore Control Room. Warehouse System: failure data. Corrective actions: owner, due date, verification. North Access Scanner: verify credential; gate secured if unverifiable; no verbal override. Southern scanner: logs; barrier closed on failure;

New part:
S954: The SCADA Engineer verifies that status, alarms, and command feedback are consistent across the available control views.
S955: The Duty Planner updates operating priorities and deferred work after the recovery status is confirmed.
S956: Normal service is restored in stages so that a successful response at one level does not conceal a remaining restriction elsewhere.
S957: The system retains the event record and recovery decisions for review, trend analysis, and improvement of operating procedures.
S958: The operating concept is governed as a controlled baseline for safe, reliable, and compliant offshore wind farm operations.
S959: The asset operator assigns an accountable owner to maintain the document and coordinate its approval.
S960: Changes to operating assumptions, responsibilities, interfaces, or decision authority require documented impact assessment before approval.
S961: The assessment considers effects on personnel safety, marine coordination, electrical safety, availability, cybersecurity, and regulatory obligations.
S962: The approved concept is consistent with applicable permits, grid requirements, safety cases, and company management systems.
S963: The Shore Control Room applies the approved operating concept during routine operations and abnormal conditions.
S964: The Control Engineer reviews control-room practices and confirms that operational procedures remain consistent with the concept.
S965: The Duty Planner checks that maintenance priorities, resource plans, and operational constraints are reflected in planned work.
S966: The Marine Coordinator reviews vessel coordination arrangements and verifies that marine responsibilities are understood.
S967: The HSE Officer evaluates safety controls, emergency arrangements, and lessons from reported events.
S968: The SCADA Engineer reviews monitoring and control assumptions that affect operational decisions.
S969: The Cybersecurity Analyst assesses changes that could affect access, communications, or the integrity of operational records.
S970: The Field Supervisor confirms that field execution practices and escalation routes are workable for offshore personnel.
S971: The Substation Operator reviews responsibilities and coordination arrangements for substation activities.
S972: Assurance evidence includes approved procedures, competence records, maintenance records, risk assessments, audit findings, and event investigations.
S973: Evidence is retained in controlled repositories with access permissions, revision history, and defined retention periods.
S974: Reviews distinguish verified evidence from assumptions, unresolved actions, and proposals that have not yet been approved.
S975: Nonconformances and operational lessons are assigned to an accountable owner with a due date and closure evidence.
S976: The document owner schedules periodic review and initiates an additional review after material operational, technical, or regulatory change.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
